label: first input token is b or f (t=0)
explanation: Fires only at step 0 when the first original token is b or f. Magnitude is essentially binary by token: f gives the max (1.718), b gives about 0.77 of max (~1.32). It does not fire on b/f at any later position, at the delimiter, or in the copy phase (except 2 negligible copy-phase activations of about 0.07 of max at the step re-inputting a first token f). Sequence length, digits and repeats do not modulate it.

issues: No systematic counterexamples. On the test split the predicate has 0 misses and 0 false positives (P=R=F1=mass recall=1.0, correlation 0.992).

On the dev split there are only 2 misses, holding 0.0% of the activation mass. Both are at step 10 with L=9, where the first token f is fed back in, and they reach 0.05-0.07 of max. This matches the stated exception.

The magnitude claim checks out. b and f fire equally often (16567 vs 16652 activations), but b holds 0.434 of the mass and f holds 0.566, so b is about 0.77x f. The median activation equals the max (1.718), which supports the near-binary claim.

Activation does not depend on L, digit count or repeats. Within each value of these, the share of activation mass tracks how often first-token b/f occurs there. Rates per step fall with L only because longer sequences have more steps.
The label matches the predicate. The only nuance is the tiny echo when f is fed back in during the copy phase, which the explanation already notes.
